correctness.rationale: The weight products telescope, and the nonzero fifth but zero sixth polynomial difference proves strict 6-isometry; the dual products are 1/P(n). Inverting the quadratic-square factor gives exp(-bt)(sin(ct)-ct cos(ct))/(2c^3). Convolution with exp(-at) is integrable even when b<a, because both factors are absolutely integrable. Under x=exp(-t) the stated finite signed density results, and polynomial density on [0,1] makes its sign necessary as well as sufficient. Its primitive has alternating extrema at the positive tan(z)=z roots. Direct substitution in the antiderivative gives the stated stationary value; Q_rho is strictly decreasing in rho even for negative rho. At rho=1/z2, Q is greater than z2/e>2. For rho at or above the threshold and z>=z2, the spatial derivative bracket splits into rho*z^2-z plus positive terms, proving that all later minima are strictly higher than the sign-controlling first minimum in the relevant comparison. This also proves exactly one interior density zero at equality and a negative open interval below it. Independent bisection gave z2=7.725251836937707 and rho*=0.18825293388019948. The frozen checker was inspected, not executed; the proof, not sampled signs, gives the universal dichotomy.

value.rationale: Coalescence of the conjugate poles is a natural boundary of the quintic problem, and pole dominance alone fails to decide it. The work completely resolves a continuous three-parameter family, supplies a single exact boundary in the normalized damping, and describes how Berger positivity is first lost. The reduction of infinitely many stationary-point conditions to a single explicit root is substantive.
